requirements.evidence: All contracted routes exist with the right methods/middleware (routes/web.php:20-51: login/register guest, logout POST auth, home auth+verified, password.request/email with throttle:6,1, password.reset/update, verification.notice/verify signed, verification.send). Login implements e-mail+password+remember, strict e-mail, auth.failed, per-e-mail+IP lockout with auth.throttle, session regenerate and redirectIntended (app/Livewire/Auth/Login.php:30-51,57-70). Register lowercases, uses unique, confirmed, Password::defaults, key str()->transliterate('register|'.ip) with 5 attempts, fires Registered, logs in, regenerates and redirects home (app/Livewire/Auth/Register.php:31-66). Reset rotates remember_token and fires PasswordReset (app/Http/Controllers/PasswordResetController.php:57-79); verification uses EmailVerificationRequest so a tampered id is 403 (app/Http/Controllers/Auth/VerifyEmailController.php:14-19); locale pins in phpunit.xml:21-22 and config/app.php. Gaps: untranslated aria-label in resources/views/components/layouts/app.blade.php:21 and the reset status flashed at PasswordResetController.php:79 is never rendered on the login page (resources/views/livewire/auth/login.blade.php:1-45).

conventions.evidence: Public input properties in app/Livewire/Auth/Login.php:17-21 and app/Livewire/Auth/Register.php:18-22 have no #[Validate] attributes and no rules() method; rules are inline in submit() (Login.php:30-33, Register.php:35-39), contradicting the project pattern 'Livewire components validate with #[Validate] + $this->validate()' (conventions.md:36-38) and Livewire policy rule 1 (conventions.md:131-133). Both new layouts duplicate the same head/asset block (resources/views/components/layouts/app.blade.php:1-20 vs guest.blade.php:1-20). Docs work was only a CHANGELOG entry (CHANGELOG.md:26); README/docs pages were not checked/updated per conventions.md:92-103.

security.evidence: All input is validated server-side before use (Login.php:30-33, Register.php:35-39, PasswordResetController.php:51-55,179-181). Login and registration are rate-limited inside the components (Login.php:57-70, Register.php:55-66); verification is signed and throttled (routes/web.php:40-42) and EmailVerificationRequest enforces id/hash ownership, so a tampered link verifies nobody (VerifyEmailController.php:14-19). Logout invalidates the session and regenerates the CSRF token (app/Http/Controllers/LogoutController.php:16-20). No {!! !!} is used; all output uses {{ }} (e.g. resources/views/home.blade.php:2-4, livewire/auth/login.blade.php:857-893). Mass assignment is bounded by #[Fillable] (app/Models/User.php:415) and User::create only receives validated fields (Register.php:41). Form actions and links go through route() (forgot-password.blade.php:641,660; layouts/app.blade.php:763,769).

tests.evidence: Six Pest suites cover the feature: login happy path/lockout/intended/remember/audit (tests/Feature/Auth/LoginTest.php), registration rules/unique/limit (RegisterTest.php), reset token/remember_token rotation/PasswordReset event (PasswordResetTest.php), home/logout (HomeAndLogoutTest.php), verification notice/tamper/403/resend (EmailVerificationTest.php:59-88), and locale/hardcoded-links (LocalizationTest.php). Meaningful tamper coverage exists for the verification link. Missing: an unauthorized-call or tamper test for the public Livewire actions Login::submit and Register::submit (required by conventions.md:183-185), and no test of the 429 on the throttled verification.verify route (routes/web.php:40-42); only resend throttling is tested (EmailVerificationTest.php:102-115).

simplicity.evidence: The change leans on framework pieces instead of reimplementing them: Password broker (PasswordResetController.php:35,57), EmailVerificationRequest (VerifyEmailController.php:19), guest/auth/verified middleware and throttle (routes/web.php:20,27,37,40,49), Password::defaults configured once (AppServiceProvider.php:24-25). Components and controllers stay small. Minor duplication: the two layouts repeat the same <head>/asset block (components/layouts/app.blade.php:1-20 and guest.blade.php:1-20).

readability.evidence: Single-purpose methods with short docblocks (Login.php:26-73, Register.php:29-66, PasswordResetController.php:27-80); consistent Bulma field/control markup and translated labels across resources/views/livewire/auth/login.blade.php and register.blade.php; route names and translation keys are descriptive (lang/en/ui.php, lang/pt_BR/ui.php). No dead code, debugging output or leftover TODOs in the diff.

scope.evidence: Almost every file serves the auth task (routes/web.php, app/Http/Controllers/*, app/Livewire/Auth/*, lang/*/ui.php, views, tests, .env.example, phpunit.xml, CHANGELOG). Extra beyond the task: audit-channel logging in the login flow (Login.php:40,65) plus its dedicated test (LoginTest.php:159-173). No unrelated refactors or out-of-scope features (mail theme, Docker, SCSS/JS untouched).

issues.explanation: The public input properties carry no #[Validate] attributes and there is no rules() method; validation happens only via inline rules in $this->validate() (Login.php:30-33, Register.php:35-39), which the project's Livewire policy rule 1 and conventions explicitly forbid.

There is no unauthorized-call or tamper test for the public submit() actions of the Login and Register components, which the Livewire definition of done requires for each action; only the guest GET redirect is tested.
The navigation aria-label is hardcoded English ('main navigation'), so assistive-tech text is not localized even though requirement 8 says all screen text must come from the translation files.
PasswordResetController.php:79 redirects to login with a status flash, but the login view never renders session('status'), so the user gets no confirmation that the password was reset.
The verification.verify route is throttled (6,1) but no test exercises its 429 response; only the resend endpoint's throttle is covered.
Audit-channel logging and its dedicated test are not requested by the task and add a small amount of unrequested behavior to the login flow.
The two layouts duplicate the same <head> and asset-loading block; a shared partial or base layout would avoid the copy-paste.

Only the CHANGELOG was updated; the new auth routes/flow were not reflected in the other docs the conventions ask to keep in sync (README/docs/architecture), or at least the change gives no evidence they were checked.

review.summary: The change adds the complete session-auth flow (login, registration, logout, password reset, e-mail verification, pt-BR/English UI) with Laravel-native primitives, server-side validation, rate limiting, signed verification links and broad Pest coverage; the security posture is strong. It falls short of merge because the Livewire components use inline validation instead of the project-mandated #[Validate]/rules() pattern and omit the required unauthorized/tamper tests for their public actions, with a few smaller localization and UX gaps.
